terms.short: Contest for the ball on the ground after a tackle, formed when at least one player from each team is on their feet and in contact over the ball.
terms.refSignal: No formal signal for formation; the referee calls 'ruck' and points the way the ball is going once it is won.
terms.whyItMatters: Most penalties happen here. Players must stay on their feet and join from behind the back foot.

terms.short: A ball carrier held by one or more opponents, with at least one teammate bound on, all on their feet and moving toward a goal line.
terms.refSignal: Referee mimes a pulling motion with both hands, then points to the side that has the ball.
terms.whyItMatters: Rolling mauls are a major try-scoring route; collapsing one is a penalty.

terms.short: The ball goes forward off a hand or arm and hits the ground or another player.
terms.refSignal: Referee moves one hand forward across the other arm in a forward-knocking motion.
terms.whyItMatters: Scrum to the other team, which changes possession.

terms.short: A pass thrown forward toward the opposition's dead-ball line.
terms.refSignal: Referee makes a forward throwing motion with both hands.
terms.whyItMatters: Scrum to the opposition. Judged on the direction of the pass, not the passer's body.

terms.short: A player in front of the back foot of the hindmost player at a ruck takes part in play.
terms.refSignal: Referee points to the offending team, then signals a penalty.
terms.whyItMatters: Penalty, often in a kickable position.

terms.short: A tackled player fails to release the ball, or a tackler fails to release the player, immediately.
terms.refSignal: Referee mimes holding the ball to the chest, then gives the penalty arm.
terms.whyItMatters: Penalty against the player holding on; one of the most common ruck penalties.

terms.short: A player uses their hands to play the ball at a ruck when they are not entitled to.
terms.refSignal: Referee mimes reaching into the ruck with a hand, then gives the penalty arm.
terms.whyItMatters: Penalty. Once a ruck has formed, players may not use their hands on the ball.

terms.short: A player prevents opponents from competing for the ball by lying across the tackled player or the ball.
terms.refSignal: Referee mimes blocking access to the ball, then gives the penalty arm.
terms.whyItMatters: Penalty. The ball must be available to both teams.

terms.short: A player obstructs a defender by running in front of or alongside the ball carrier, or a player in a maul, without being bound.
terms.refSignal: Referee signals obstruction (arm across the body), then the penalty arm.
terms.whyItMatters: Penalty against the team that blocks the defenders.

terms.short: A kick from inside the kicker's own half that bounces and then goes into touch inside the opposition 22; the kicking team throws in at the lineout.
terms.refSignal: Referee signals the lineout throw to the kicking team.
terms.whyItMatters: Gives the kicking team territory and the throw-in.

terms.short: Restart where a kick is held up or made dead in the in-goal by the defending side; the defenders restart with a drop kick from the 22.
terms.refSignal: Referee points to the 22 and signals a dropout.
terms.whyItMatters: Returns the ball to the defenders at the 22.

terms.short: Television Match Official who reviews video to help the referee with tries, foul play and certain other incidents.
terms.refSignal: Referee draws a TV screen shape in the air with both hands.
terms.whyItMatters: Final try and foul-play decisions can depend on the review.

terms.short: A review of potential red-card incidents by a separate official while play continues, used in competitions that apply the 20-minute red card.
terms.refSignal: Referee shows a card or signals the review, depending on the competition.
terms.whyItMatters: Can upgrade or downgrade a card without the match being held up for a long time.

terms.short: A red card where the offender is sent off but the team may replace them after 20 minutes. Used in some competitions.
terms.refSignal: Referee shows the red card.
terms.whyItMatters: The team is a player short for 20 minutes, then back to 15.

terms.short: The referee lets play continue after an offence if the non-offending team can gain a clear benefit.
terms.refSignal: Referee extends one arm toward the non-offending team and calls 'advantage'.
terms.whyItMatters: If there is no clear gain, play comes back for the original penalty or scrum.

terms.short: A catch directly from an opponent's kick, made on or inside the catcher's own 22, with a call of 'mark'.
terms.refSignal: Referee signals a free kick to the catcher.
terms.whyItMatters: Gives the catcher a free kick.

terms.short: A front row deliberately or repeatedly pulls the scrum down.
terms.refSignal: Referee mimes the scrum going down, then gives a penalty or free kick.
terms.whyItMatters: Penalty against the side at fault; repeated collapses can bring a card.

terms.short: Offences at the scrum such as early engagement, boring in, standing up or pulling an opponent down.
terms.refSignal: Referee signals the offence, then the penalty arm toward the non-offending side.
terms.whyItMatters: Penalty or free kick, which can mean a shot at goal.

terms.short: The thrower fails to throw the ball straight down the middle of the lineout.
terms.refSignal: Referee mimes the throw with a crooked arm.
terms.whyItMatters: Scrum to the opposition (or a free kick in some cases).

terms.short: World Rugby's tackle framework that sets the sanction for head contact, based on the degree of danger and mitigation.
terms.refSignal: Referee mimes contact to the head, then shows a yellow or red card where needed.
terms.whyItMatters: It explains why a high tackle may be a penalty, yellow card or red card.

terms.short: A player intentionally knocks the ball forward to stop an opponent gaining an advantage.
terms.refSignal: Referee mimes the knock-on, then gives the penalty arm.
terms.whyItMatters: Penalty, and often a yellow card if it stops a probable try.

terms.short: A tackle made at or above the line of the shoulders.
terms.refSignal: Referee touches the chest, shoulder or neck area, then gives the penalty arm.
terms.whyItMatters: Penalty; yellow or red card depending on the severity.

terms.short: A player who stays on their feet over the ball after a tackle and tries to win a turnover.
terms.refSignal: No signal; the referee watches that the player supports their own weight.
terms.whyItMatters: A major turnover tool; if the jackal goes off their feet or enters from the side, it is a penalty.

terms.short: A clean-out where a player grabs a leg or hip of an opponent over the ball and rolls them away.
terms.refSignal: Referee mimes the rolling motion, then gives the penalty arm.
terms.whyItMatters: Penalised as dangerous play and can lead to a card.

terms.short: Head Injury Assessment: an off-field concussion check, with a temporary replacement allowed during it.
terms.refSignal: Referee stops play; the HIA is signalled by the medical team.
terms.whyItMatters: A failed HIA means the player does not return.

terms.short: A 10-minute temporary suspension.
terms.refSignal: Referee holds a yellow card above their head.
terms.whyItMatters: The team plays a player short for 10 minutes.

terms.short: Permanent send-off for serious foul play.
terms.refSignal: Referee holds a red card above their head.
terms.whyItMatters: The player cannot return; the team is down a player (subject to competition rules).

terms.short: Awarded when the referee decides a try would probably have been scored but for foul play.
terms.refSignal: Referee runs under the posts with both arms raised.
terms.whyItMatters: 7 points with no conversion; the offender is often carded.

terms.short: A kick at goal after a try, taken in line with where the ball was grounded.
terms.refSignal: Referee signals the kick with a raised arm.
terms.whyItMatters: Worth 2 points.

terms.short: A kick at goal in open play where the ball bounces off the ground just before it is kicked.
terms.refSignal: Referee raises both arms.
terms.whyItMatters: Worth 3 points.

terms.short: A kick at goal from the place of the penalty.
terms.refSignal: Referee raises both arms.
terms.whyItMatters: Worth 3 points.

terms.short: The ball is grounded in the opponent's in-goal area by an attacker.
terms.refSignal: Referee raises one arm and points to the posts or to the grounding.
terms.whyItMatters: Worth 5 points plus a conversion attempt.

terms.short: Eight forwards from each team bind and push for the ball after a minor offence or stoppage.
terms.refSignal: Referee points to the team that puts the ball in.
terms.whyItMatters: Restart after knock-ons and forward passes.

terms.short: Restart after the ball goes into touch, with jumpers lifted by teammates.
terms.refSignal: Referee points toward the team that throws in.
terms.whyItMatters: A set-piece for attack and a source of mauls.

terms.short: A restart for a minor offence; the opposing team must retreat 10 m.
terms.refSignal: Referee bends one arm at the elbow and raises it.
terms.whyItMatters: No shot at goal; the team may kick, run or tap.

terms.short: A quick restart after a penalty without waiting for a kick.
terms.refSignal: Referee points toward the team and then lets play start.
terms.whyItMatters: Allows a fast attack.

terms.short: A penalty or free kick kicked out to touch to gain territory.
terms.refSignal: Referee points toward the touchline and signals a lineout.
terms.whyItMatters: Gains territory with the throw-in.

terms.short: A player in front of a teammate who last played the ball takes part in play.
terms.refSignal: Referee points to the offending team, then gives the penalty arm.
terms.whyItMatters: Penalty to the other team.

terms.short: A player gets in the way of an opponent who is not the ball carrier.
terms.refSignal: Referee crosses the arms in front of the chest, then gives the penalty arm.
terms.whyItMatters: Penalty.

terms.short: Play that puts another player at risk, such as lifting a player past the horizontal.
terms.refSignal: Referee mimes the offence, then shows a card where needed.
terms.whyItMatters: Penalty and possible yellow or red card.

terms.short: Challenging or tackling a player who is in the air.
terms.refSignal: Referee mimes the contact in the air and gives the penalty arm.
terms.whyItMatters: Penalty; often a card because of the landing.

terms.short: Informal name for the 10-minute yellow card suspension.
terms.refSignal: Referee shows a yellow card.
terms.whyItMatters: The player waits off the field for 10 minutes.

terms.short: A player moves early or stands in the wrong place at a lineout.
terms.refSignal: Referee points to the offside line and gives the penalty arm.
terms.whyItMatters: Penalty or free kick.

terms.short: Deliberately pulling a maul down.
terms.refSignal: Referee mimes the maul going down, then gives the penalty arm.
terms.whyItMatters: Penalty; possible yellow card.

terms.short: A deliberate foul to stop an attack, such as slowing the ball or pulling down a maul.
terms.refSignal: Referee signals the offence, then shows a yellow card.
terms.whyItMatters: Yellow card (or red for the most serious).

terms.short: A player accidentally ends offside and gains no advantage.
terms.refSignal: Referee signals a scrum to the other team.
terms.whyItMatters: Scrum, no penalty.

terms.short: The ball goes beyond the dead-ball line or touch-in-goal.
terms.refSignal: Referee signals a 22 dropout or a scrum, depending on the incident.
terms.whyItMatters: Play restarts with a 22 dropout or a scrum.

terms.short: A pass that goes forward leaves receivers offside until play restarts.
terms.refSignal: Referee signals the forward pass.
terms.whyItMatters: Scrum to the other team.

terms.short: Referee plays advantage but comes back if there is no gain.
terms.refSignal: Referee holds out one arm toward the non-offending team.
terms.whyItMatters: Play on or penalty.

decisions.signal: One hand moves forward across the other arm
Both hands thrust forward as if throwing
One arm raised and angled toward the non-offending team
decisions.outcome: Kick at goal, touch or tap

decisions.signal: One arm bent at the elbow and raised
decisions.outcome: Tap or kick; no direct goal attempt

decisions.signal: One arm extended toward the non-offending team
decisions.outcome: Play on; back to the penalty if no gain

decisions.signal: One arm raised, then pointing to the grounding
Both arms raised and referee under the posts
Arm pointing to the feeding team
Arm pointing to the throwing team
Hand touching the shoulder or neck area
decisions.outcome: Penalty; yellow or red card if severe

decisions.signal: Arm pointing to the offender and the offside line
Mimes holding the ball to the chest
Yellow card held above the head
Red card held above the head
decisions.outcome: Sent off for the match (or 20-minute red card)

decisions.signal: Both hands draw a TV screen in the air
decisions.outcome: Video check before the decision is final
